History of Morocco.fact: Up until the 14th century, as the northern terminus for the western trans-Sahara trade route, it was one of the most important trade centres in the Maghreb during the Middle Ages.

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages
History of Morocco.question: He first arrived in Tangier, the most important city of Morocco at the time, and by _____ he had settled in Volubilis (known as Walili in Arabic)
History of Morocco.fact: The founder of the Idrisid dynasty was Idris ibn Abdallah (788–791), who traced his ancestry back to Ali ibn Abi Talib (died 661) and his wife Fatimah, daughter of the Islamic prophet, Muhammad. He first arrived in Tangier, the most important city of Morocco at the time, and by 788 he had settled in Volubilis (known as Walili in Arabic).

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages
History of Morocco.question: By the second half of the _____th century they had settled in northern Morocco, where their leader Ishak had his base in the Roman town of Volubilis
History of Morocco.fact: He first arrived in Tangier, the most important city of Morocco at the time, and by 788 he had settled in Volubilis (known as Walili in Arabic). The Awraba tribe had supported Kusayla in his struggle against the Umayyad armies in the 670s and 680s.

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages
History of Morocco.question: His brother Isa, who was given control of the coastal Tamesna regions near the _____ from his base at Chellah, quickly revolted against him
History of Morocco.fact: His brother Isa, who was given control of the coastal Tamesna regions near the Bou Regreg from his base at Chellah, quickly revolted against him.

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages
History of Morocco.question: Muhammad entrusted his brother _____, who had received the territories around the Rif, to punish Isa
History of Morocco.fact: Muhammad entrusted his brother Umar, who had received the territories around the Rif, to punish Isa. Umar successfully drove Isa from power, who was forced to take refuge in Chellah, and then turned north to punish his other brother al-Qasim at Tangier because he had earlier refused to join him and Muhammad against Isa.

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages
History of Morocco.question: Al-Qasim fled to _____ and settled nearby, while Muhammad gave Umar governorship of Tangier as a reward
History of Morocco.fact: Al-Qasim fled to Asilah and settled nearby, while Muhammad gave Umar governorship of Tangier as a reward.

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages
History of Morocco.question: Muhammad himself died seven months later in the _____ or April 836
History of Morocco.fact: Muhammad himself died seven months later in the March or April 836.

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages
History of Morocco.question: His son Ali ibn _____ inherited his position and ruled for 13 years (836–849) in a competent manner, ensuring the stability of the state
History of Morocco.fact: Al-Qasim fled to Asilah and settled nearby, while Muhammad gave Umar governorship of Tangier as a reward. Muhammad himself died seven months later in the March or April 836.

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages
History of Morocco.question: After his death in 849 he was succeeded by his brother Yahya ibn _____ (or Yahya I), who also enjoyed a peaceful reign
History of Morocco.fact: Muhammad himself died seven months later in the March or April 836. His son Ali ibn Muhammad inherited his position and ruled for 13 years (836–849) in a competent manner, ensuring the stability of the state.

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages
History of Morocco.question: During this time _____ and Arabic culture gained a stronghold in the towns and Morocco profited from the trans-Saharan trade, which came to be dominated by Muslim (mostly Berber) traders
History of Morocco.fact: During this time Islamic and Arabic culture gained a stronghold in the towns and Morocco profited from the trans-Saharan trade, which came to be dominated by Muslim (mostly Berber) traders. Even so, the Islamic and Arabic culture only made its influence felt in the towns, with the vast majority of Morocco's population still using the Berber languages and often adhering to Islamic heterodox and heretical doctrines.

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages
History of Morocco.question: After an episode of disorder in Fes his cousin Ali ibn _____ took over power
History of Morocco.fact: After an episode of disorder in Fes his cousin Ali ibn Umar took over power. From their base in Sefrou they were able to defeat Ali ibn Umar and occupy Fes.

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages
History of Morocco.question: In 868, under the leadership of the Abd al-Razzaq the _____ tribes of Madyuna, Ghayata and Miknasa of the Fes region formed a common front against the Idrisids
History of Morocco.fact: In 868, under the leadership of the Abd al-Razzaq the Berber Khariji Sufri tribes of Madyuna, Ghayata and Miknasa of the Fes region formed a common front against the Idrisids.

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages
History of Morocco.question: From their base in _____ they were able to defeat Ali ibn Umar and occupy Fes
History of Morocco.fact: From their base in Sefrou they were able to defeat Ali ibn Umar and occupy Fes.

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages
History of Morocco.question: Fes refused to submit, however, and another _____, the son of al-Qasim, was able to retake the city and establish himself as the new ruler, Yahya III
History of Morocco.fact: Fes refused to submit, however, and another Yahya, the son of al-Qasim, was able to retake the city and establish himself as the new ruler, Yahya III. Yahya III ruled over the entire Idrisid realm and continued to attack the Sufris.

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages
History of Morocco.question: In 905 however he died in battle against another family member, _____ ibn Idris ibn Umar (a grandson of Umar), who then took power as Yahya IV
History of Morocco.fact: Fes refused to submit, however, and another Yahya, the son of al-Qasim, was able to retake the city and establish himself as the new ruler, Yahya III. Yahya III ruled over the entire Idrisid realm and continued to attack the Sufris.

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages
History of Morocco.question: Thus the ruling line had passed from the sons of _____ to the son of Umar and now the sons of al-Qasim
History of Morocco.fact: Thus the ruling line had passed from the sons of Muhammad to the son of Umar and now the sons of al-Qasim.

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages
History of Morocco.question: Yahya III ruled over the entire _____ realm and continued to attack the Sufris
History of Morocco.fact: Yahya III ruled over the entire Idrisid realm and continued to attack the Sufris.

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages
History of Morocco.question: At this point, however, the _____ in the east began to intervene in Morocco, hoping to expand their influence
History of Morocco.fact: At this point, however, the Fatimids in the east began to intervene in Morocco, hoping to expand their influence.

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages
History of Morocco.question: In 917 the _____ and its leader Masala ibn Habus, acting on behalf of their Fatimid allies, attacked Fes and forced Yahya IV to recognize Fatimid suzerainty, before deposing him in 919 or 921
History of Morocco.fact: In 917 the Miknasa and its leader Masala ibn Habus, acting on behalf of their Fatimid allies, attacked Fes and forced Yahya IV to recognize Fatimid suzerainty, before deposing him in 919 or 921. From Fes, the Miknasa began pursuing the Idrisid family across Morocco.

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages
History of Morocco.question: From Fes, the _____ began pursuing the Idrisid family across Morocco
History of Morocco.fact: In 917 the Miknasa and its leader Masala ibn Habus, acting on behalf of their Fatimid allies, attacked Fes and forced Yahya IV to recognize Fatimid suzerainty, before deposing him in 919 or 921. From Fes, the Miknasa began pursuing the Idrisid family across Morocco.

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages
History of Morocco.question: He was succeeded by his cousin _____ ibn Abul 'Afiya, who had already been given charge over the rest of the country
History of Morocco.fact: He was succeeded by his cousin Musa ibn Abul 'Afiya, who had already been given charge over the rest of the country. The Idrisid Hassan I al-Hajam, a grandson of al-Qasim, managed to wrest control of Fez from 925 but in 927 Musa returned, captured Hassan and killed him, marking the last time the Idrisids held power in Fes.

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages
History of Morocco.question: The family took refuge at the fortress of Hajar an-Nasr in northern Morocco, where the _____ besieged them
History of Morocco.fact: From Fes, the Miknasa began pursuing the Idrisid family across Morocco. The family took refuge at the fortress of Hajar an-Nasr in northern Morocco, where the Miknasa besieged them.

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages
History of Morocco.question: Soon after, however, civil war broke out among the _____ when Musa switched allegiance to the Umayyads of Cordoba in 931 in an attempt to gain more independence
History of Morocco.fact: From Fes, the Miknasa began pursuing the Idrisid family across Morocco. The family took refuge at the fortress of Hajar an-Nasr in northern Morocco, where the Miknasa besieged them.

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages
History of Morocco.question: The Fatimids sent _____ ibn Yasal (or Hamid), the nephew of Masala ibn Habus, to confront Musa, defeating him in 933 and forcing him to fall back into line
History of Morocco.fact: The Fatimids sent Humayd ibn Yasal (or Hamid), the nephew of Masala ibn Habus, to confront Musa, defeating him in 933 and forcing him to fall back into line.

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages
History of Morocco.question: The Idrisids took advantage of the situation to break the siege of their fortress and defeat the _____ troops
History of Morocco.fact: The Idrisids took advantage of the situation to break the siege of their fortress and defeat the Mikanasa Zenata troops.

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages
History of Morocco.question: Once the _____ were gone, however, Musa once again threw off their authority and recognized the Umayyad caliph
History of Morocco.fact: The Fatimids sent Humayd ibn Yasal (or Hamid), the nephew of Masala ibn Habus, to confront Musa, defeating him in 933 and forcing him to fall back into line. Once the Fatimids were gone, however, Musa once again threw off their authority and recognized the Umayyad caliph.

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages

History of Morocco.fact: The Fatimids sent their general Maysur to confront him again, and this time he fled.

History of Morocco.question: He was pursued and killed by the _____
History of Morocco.fact: The Idrisids took advantage of the situation to break the siege of their fortress and defeat the Mikanasa Zenata troops. He was pursued and killed by the Idrisids.

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages
History of Morocco.question: Al-Qasim al-_____ ibn Muhammad ruled here from 938 until 948 in the name of the Fatimids
History of Morocco.fact: Al-Qasim al-Gannoun ibn Muhammad ruled here from 938 until 948 in the name of the Fatimids. He eventually left for Al-Andalus, leaving his brother Hasan ibn al-Qasim al-Gannoun as the new leader in 954.

History of Morocco.fact: In 958 the Fatimids sent a new general, Jawhar, to invade Morocco. Soon afterwards, however, when Jawhar and the Fatimids were busy taking control of Egypt, the Umayyads made a comeback.

History of Morocco.fact: In 958 the Fatimids sent a new general, Jawhar, to invade Morocco. Soon afterwards, however, when Jawhar and the Fatimids were busy taking control of Egypt, the Umayyads made a comeback.

History of Morocco.fact: The Idrisids were expelled from their territories and al-Hasan, along with many other Idrisids or their sons, were taken as hostages to Cordoba in 974. The remaining Idrisids in Morocco acknowledged Umayyad rule.

History of Morocco.question: Al-Hasan was later expelled from _____ and fled to Egypt, which was now under Fatimid rule
History of Morocco.fact: The Idrisids were expelled from their territories and al-Hasan, along with many other Idrisids or their sons, were taken as hostages to Cordoba in 974. Al-Hasan was later expelled from Cordoba and fled to Egypt, which was now under Fatimid rule.

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages
History of Morocco.question: In 985 he returned to Morocco with _____ support, but that same year he was defeated by another Umayyad general sent by al-Mansur and then assassinated on the way to Cordoba
History of Morocco.fact: Al-Hasan was later expelled from Cordoba and fled to Egypt, which was now under Fatimid rule. In 979 Buluggin ibn Ziri, the Fatimid governor of Ifriqiya (after the Fatimid Caliphs moved their capital to Cairo), returned to defeat the Umayyads and impose Fatimid overlordship in the western Maghreb again.

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages
History of Morocco.question: This brought a final end to the _____ dynasty
History of Morocco.fact: This brought a final end to the Idrisid dynasty.

History of Morocco.fact: Following this, Morocco was dominated by various Zenata Berber tribes.

History of Morocco.fact: The conquest of the city of Marrakesh by the Almohads in 1147 marked the fall of the dynasty.

History of Morocco.fact: However, fragments of the Almoravids (the Banu Ghaniya) continued to struggle in the Balearic Islands and in Tunisia.

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages

History of Morocco.fact: The Berbers of the Tamazgha in the early Middle Ages could be roughly classified into three major groups: the Zenata across the north, the Masmuda concentrated in central Morocco, and the Sanhaja, clustered in two areas: the western part of the Sahara and the hills of the eastern Maghreb. History of Morocco.fact: They were subsequently united in the 10th century and, with the zeal of new converts, launched several campaigns against the "Sudanese" (pagan peoples of sub-Saharan Africa).

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages
History of Morocco.question: Under their king _____ ibn Usfayshar, the Sanhaja Lamtuna erected (or captured) the citadel of Awdaghust, a critical stop on the trans-Saharan trade route
History of Morocco.fact: Under their king Tinbarutan ibn Usfayshar, the Sanhaja Lamtuna erected (or captured) the citadel of Awdaghust, a critical stop on the trans-Saharan trade route.

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages

History of Morocco.fact: The western Sanhaja had been converted to Islam some time in the 9th century. Under their king Tinbarutan ibn Usfayshar, the Sanhaja Lamtuna erected (or captured) the citadel of Awdaghust, a critical stop on the trans-Saharan trade route.

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages

History of Morocco.fact: The Maghrawa also exploited this disunion to dislodge the Sanhaja Gazzula and Lamta out of their pasturelands in the Sous and Draa valleys.

History of Morocco.fact: Around 1035, the Lamtuna chieftain Abu Abdallah Muhammad ibn Tifat (alias Tarsina), tried to reunite the Sanhaja desert tribes, but his reign lasted less than three years.

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages
History of Morocco.question: Around _____, Yahya ibn Ibrahim, a chieftain of the Gudala (and brother-in-law of the late Tarsina), went on pilgrimage to Mecca
History of Morocco.fact: Around 1040, Yahya ibn Ibrahim, a chieftain of the Gudala (and brother-in-law of the late Tarsina), went on pilgrimage to Mecca.

History of Morocco.fact: The Zirid ruler al-Muizz ibn Badis, was openly contemplating breaking with his Shi'ite Fatimid overlords in Cairo, and the jurists of Kairouan were agitating for him to do so.

History of Morocco.fact: Waggag assigned him one of his residents, Abdallah ibn Yasin. Abdallah ibn Yasin was a Gazzula Berber, and probably a convert rather than a born Muslim.

History of Morocco.fact: Abdallah ibn Yasin was a Gazzula Berber, and probably a convert rather than a born Muslim.

History of Morocco.fact: His name can be read as "son of Ya Sin" (the title of the 36th Sura of the Qur'an), suggesting he had obliterated his family past and was "re-born" of the Holy Book.

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages

History of Morocco.fact: Ibn Yasin certainly had the ardor of a puritan zealot; his creed was mainly characterized by a rigid formalism and a strict adherence to the dictates of the Qur'an, and the Orthodox tradition.

History of Morocco.fact: Ibn Yasin certainly had the ardor of a puritan zealot; his creed was mainly characterized by a rigid formalism and a strict adherence to the dictates of the Qur'an, and the Orthodox tradition. (Chroniclers such as al-Bakri allege Ibn Yasin's learning was superficial.) Ibn Yasin's initial meetings with the Gudala people went poorly.

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages

History of Morocco.fact: The Gudala soon had enough and expelled him almost immediately after the death of his protector, Yahya ibn Ibrahim, sometime in the 1040s.

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages
History of Morocco.question: Ibn Yasin, however, found a more favorable reception among the neighboring _____ people
History of Morocco.fact: Ibn Yasin, however, found a more favorable reception among the neighboring Lamtuna people. Probably sensing the useful organizing power of Ibn Yasin's pious fervor, the Lamtuna chieftain Yahya ibn Umar al-Lamtuni invited the man to preach to his people.

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages
History of Morocco.question: Probably sensing the useful organizing power of _____'s pious fervor, the Lamtuna chieftain Yahya ibn Umar al-Lamtuni invited the man to preach to his people
History of Morocco.fact: Ibn Yasin, however, found a more favorable reception among the neighboring Lamtuna people. Probably sensing the useful organizing power of Ibn Yasin's pious fervor, the Lamtuna chieftain Yahya ibn Umar al-Lamtuni invited the man to preach to his people.

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages

History of Morocco.fact: 'those who profess the unity of God') was a North African Berber Muslim empire set up in present day Morocco at the 12th century.

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages
History of Morocco.question: At its height, it controlled much of the _____ (Al Andalus) and North Africa (the Maghreb)
History of Morocco.fact: At its height, it controlled much of the Iberian Peninsula (Al Andalus) and North Africa (the Maghreb).

History of Morocco.subject: Indian Languages

Zaian War.fact: In Spring 1922, Poeymirau and Freydenberg launched attacks into the headwaters of the Moulouya in the western Middle Atlas and managed to defeat Said, the last surviving member of the Berber triumvirate, at El Ksiba in April 1922. Lyautey then secured the submission of several more tribes, constructed new military posts and improved his supply roads; by June 1922, he had brought the entire Moulouya Valley under control and pacified much of the Middle Atlas.

Zaian War.subject: Indian Languages
Zaian War.question: Said was forced to flee, with much of the Aït _____ tribe, to the highest mountains of the Middle Atlas and then into the High Atlas
Zaian War.fact: Said was forced to flee, with much of the Aït Ichkern tribe, to the highest mountains of the Middle Atlas and then into the High Atlas.

Zaian War.subject: Indian Languages
Zaian War.question: Said never did so, dying in action against a groupe mobile in March _____, though his followers continued to cause problems for the French into the next decade
Zaian War.fact: Said never did so, dying in action against a groupe mobile in March 1924, though his followers continued to cause problems for the French into the next decade.

Zaian War.subject: Indian Languages
Zaian War.question: Pacification of the remaining tribal areas in French Morocco was completed in _____, though small armed gangs of bandits continued to attack French troops in the mountains until 1936
Zaian War.fact: Pacification of the remaining tribal areas in French Morocco was completed in 1934, though small armed gangs of bandits continued to attack French troops in the mountains until 1936. Moroccan opposition to French rule continued, a plan for reform and return to indirect rule was published by the nationalist Comité d'Action Marocaine (CAM) in 1934, with significant riots and demonstrations occurring in 1934, 1937, 1944 and 1951.

Zaian War.subject: Indian Languages
Zaian War.question: France, having failed to quell the nationalists by deposing the popular Sultan Mohammed V and already fighting a bloody war of independence in Algeria, recognised Moroccan independence in _____
Zaian War.fact: France, having failed to quell the nationalists by deposing the popular Sultan Mohammed V and already fighting a bloody war of independence in Algeria, recognised Moroccan independence in 1956.

Zaian War.subject: Indian Languages
Zaian War.question: Lyautey was offered the post of Minister of War at the invitation of _____, which he accepted on 12 December 1916
Zaian War.fact: Lyautey was offered the post of Minister of War at the invitation of Prime Minister Aristide Briand, which he accepted on 12 December 1916.

Zaian War.subject: Indian Languages
Zaian War.question: Local tribes resisted the _____ presence, killing a translator working at the mission in July 1918
Zaian War.fact: Doury had expanded the theatre of operations, against Lyautey's orders, by establishing a French mission at Tighmart, in the Tafilalt region, in December 1917 in reaction to a rumoured German presence there. The land here, mainly desert, was almost worthless to the French and Lyautey was keen for his subordinates to focus on the more valuable Moulouya Valley.

Zaian War.subject: Indian Languages
Zaian War.question: A series of commercial expositions, such as the _____ of 1915, were held to demonstrate the wealth of France and the benefits of co-operation
Zaian War.fact: A series of commercial expositions, such as the Casablanca Fair of 1915, were held to demonstrate the wealth of France and the benefits of co-operation.

Zaian War.subject: Indian Languages
Zaian War.question: Lyautey then received assistance from _____, a tribal leader who Lyautey had made Pasha of Marrakesh after the uprising of 1912
Zaian War.fact: Lyautey then received assistance from Thami El Glaoui, a tribal leader who Lyautey had made Pasha of Marrakesh after the uprising of 1912.

Zaian War.question: The Moroccans pressed to within 50 metres (55 yards) of the French, and _____-Duplessix, in command of the convoy, was forced to resort to the bayonet to push them back
Zaian War.fact: In recognition of this Garnier-Duplessix was promoted to major-general. The Moroccans pressed to within 50 metres (55 yards) of the French, and Garnier-Duplessix, in command of the convoy, was forced to resort to the bayonet to push them back.

Zaian War.subject: Indian Languages
Zaian War.question: These problems led many of the _____ diplomatic corps in Spain to leave for America in September 1916, bringing to an end many of the significant Ottoman operations in Morocco
Zaian War.fact: Much of the Ottoman intelligence effort was coordinated by Arab agents operating from the embassy in Madrid and at least two members of the Ottoman diplomatic staff there are known to have seen active service with the tribes in Morocco during the war. Ottoman efforts in Morocco were hindered by internal divisions among the staff, disagreements with their German allies and the outbreak of the Arab Revolt in 1916, with which some of the embassy staff sympathised.

Zaian War.subject: Indian Languages
Zaian War.question: By October the situation had stabilised to the extent that _____ was able to withdraw his troops to Meknes, but a large-scale uprising in January 1919 forced his return
Zaian War.fact: Poeymirau was forced to withdraw garrisons from outlying posts in the Tafilalt, including that at Tighmart, to concentrate his force and reduce the risk of further disasters. By October the situation had stabilised to the extent that Poeymirau was able to withdraw his troops to Meknes, but a large-scale uprising in January 1919 forced his return.

Zaian War.subject: Indian Languages
Zaian War.question: The uprising was over by 31 _____ 1919
Zaian War.fact: Thus committed to Lyautey's cause, El Glaoui led an army of 10,000 men, the largest Moroccan tribal force ever seen, across the Atlas to defeat anti-French tribesmen in the Dadès Gorges and to reinforce the garrison at Boudenib on 29 January. The uprising was over by 31 January 1919.

Zaian War.subject: Indian Languages
Zaian War.question: The French continued to hope for a negotiated end to the conflict and had been in discussions with _____'s close relatives since 1917
Zaian War.fact: The French continued to hope for a negotiated end to the conflict and had been in discussions with Hammou's close relatives since 1917. Indeed, his nephew, Ou El Aidi, had offered his submission in exchange for weapons and money but had been refused by the French who suspected he wanted to fight with his cousin, Hammou's son, Hassan.

Zaian War.subject: Indian Languages
Zaian War.question: With no progress in these negotiations _____ moved against the tribes to the north and south of Khénifra in 1920, the front in this area having remained static for six years
Zaian War.fact: With no progress in these negotiations Poeymirau moved against the tribes to the north and south of Khénifra in 1920, the front in this area having remained static for six years.

Zaian War.subject: Indian Languages
Zaian War.question: French successes in the Khénifra region persuaded _____ and his two brothers to submit to the French on 2 June 1920, having returned some of the equipment captured at El Herri
Zaian War.fact: French successes in the Khénifra region persuaded Hassan and his two brothers to submit to the French on 2 June 1920, having returned some of the equipment captured at El Herri. Hassan was soon appointed Pasha of Khénifra and his 3,000 tents were brought under French protection in an expanded zone of occupation around the Rbia.
